claim: Inventory walk #7 gap G24 (proposal F-C, lane I5): migration a_lot_cost_keeps_small_units widens inventory_lots.unit_cost and inventory_transactions.unit_cost from numeric(10,2) to numeric(14,6) and rewrites the WAC rounding of inventory_lot_rollup and inventory_location_breakdown from 2 to 6 places, so a per-gram lot cost of 0.035 is kept instead of read as 0.04; and no later migration recreates either view with 2-place WAC rounding or narrows unit_cost back to numeric(10,2). Behaviour is proven by supabase/tests/<version>_a_lot_cost_keeps_small_units_test.sql on local Postgres (fails on origin/main 259feea3f: T1 numeric(10,2), T2 0.04); this verify checks the migration's shape and that nothing after it undoes it.
verify: python3 -c "import glob,re,sys; fs=sorted(glob.glob('supabase/migrations/*.sql')); m=[f for f in fs if f.endswith('_a_lot_cost_keeps_small_units.sql')]; s=open(m[0]).read() if len(m)==1 else ''; later=[f for f in fs if m and f>m[0] and re.search(r'VIEW public[.]inventory_(lot_rollup|location_breakdown) AS[^;]*numeric[)], 2[)]|unit_cost TYPE numeric[(]10,2[)]', open(f).read())]; sys.exit(0 if s.count('unit_cost TYPE numeric(14,6)')==2 and chr(39)+', 6)' in s and len(glob.glob('supabase/tests/*_a_lot_cost_keeps_small_units_test.sql'))==1 and not later else 1)"
